D004-D010_h023.question:
I’m an automotive engineer, so I’m used to thinking in systems and probabilities, but this… doesn’t feel like just worry or overthinking.

For the past few months, I’ve had this growing sense that something huge and destructive is coming. Not like climate change in a general way, but more like the world is winding down, like everything is about to collapse or get wiped out. When I’m at the test track, watching the cars run, I keep catching myself thinking, “What’s the point of refining braking systems if none of this will exist soon?” It feels less like a fear and more like a certainty some days.

Around the same time, my energy’s been all over the place. Some weeks I’m buzzing—sleeping three, four hours and still going to work early, taking on extra projects, talking fast in meetings because I feel like I have to get all my ideas out before… whatever happens. Then it’ll ease up a bit, but that sense of impending catastrophe doesn’t fully go away; it just gets quieter. I’m not sure if they’re connected or if I’m just reading too much into it.

I’ve been really worried about my body for a while now. It started maybe… a few months ago? Time’s kind of blurry. I’m in culinary school, so I’m around food all day, but I keep feeling like something inside me is wrong, like there’s some kind of growth or infection in my stomach that the doctors are missing. I can almost feel it moving sometimes, like my organs aren’t arranged right. I’ve had tests, but I’m sure they overlooked something. When I’m in lab, I’ll be plating a dish and suddenly I can’t focus because I’m imagining my insides rotting or changing shape.

Around the same time, my energy’s been all over the place. Some days I barely sleep and still feel wired, talking really fast, starting new recipe ideas at 3 a.m., convinced I’m on the verge of creating something huge, like I’m meant to be some kind of famous chef. Other times I calm down a bit, but this feeling that my body is fundamentally messed up doesn’t really leave. I’m not really sure when this started, maybe a few months ago? It kind of crept up. I’ve always been good at my job, but lately it feels… bigger than that. When I’m working with the kids, it’s like I can see things in their brains other therapists just can’t. I catch myself thinking I’m supposed to revolutionize how speech therapy is done worldwide, like I’m the one who’s going to change the whole field. 

It doesn’t feel like just confidence—more like a certainty that I have this unique gift other people don’t. Sometimes I’ll be writing notes and I’ll think, “These could end up in textbooks someday,” and it seems obvious, not exaggerated. I’ve even thought the hospital might try to fast-track me into some kind of leadership role because of how special my skills are, even though no one’s actually said that.

My husband says I’m “amped up” lately—talking more, sleeping less, bouncing between ideas—but I don’t feel out of control, just very driven and important. I can’t tell if this is just me finally realizing my potential, or if something’s off.
